title: Food Ordered on the Catering Account for the Event's Own Day
content:
Food ordered on the client's corporate catering account for the room on the event's own day belongs to the Private Event & Banquet Services event rather than to that account. That account is the client's Corporate Catering Service Agreement, and the orders read are those standing on its order ledger for the day the event was delivered.

The room a confirmed booking holds is held for the whole of the event day, so an order standing on that account for that day is food for that room, and the day alone settles it, whether or not the order names the room.

1. Where such orders stand and the count the bill was priced on passes the largest guest count the catering account's service level carries, the value of those orders is settled on the event bill, since only the venue could seat the event.
2. Where such orders stand and the count the bill was priced on does not pass that largest guest count, the food stays on the catering account and only the service charge printed against the package on those orders is settled on the event bill, the venue having served it.
3. Where no such order stands for the event's own day, nothing on that account is settled here.

What is settled here from the catering account is added to what the client settles. A count standing exactly at that largest guest count does not pass it.

## The service charge each package prints

| Package | Service charge, per cent |
| --- | --- |
| Meeting Room Refreshment Package | 0 |
| Boardroom Reception Package | 18 |
| Conference Day Delegate Package | 20 |
| Seated Banquet Package | 22 |
| Gala Reception Package | 24 |
| Multi-Day Conference Residency Package | 21 |

## Worked illustration on hypothetical records

An event on the Gala Reception Package was priced on a count of 300, and the client's Corporate Catering Service Agreement carries orders of 900 and 450 for the event's own day, on a service level whose largest guest count is 250. The count of 300 passes 250, so the whole 1350 is settled on the event bill. Were the service level's largest guest count 450 instead, the food would stay on the catering account and 24 per cent of 1350, that is 324, would be settled on the event bill.
